record.file_problem: Text is a web-page extraction of an interactive essay: figures, widgets and tables are flattened or missing, and footnote 1 (which presumably explains the audit method) is not present. The Qwen3-32B audit has no method, sample size or error bars in this text. It points to a companion technical paper that is not supplied.
record.tranche_reason: This essay is the original source of the claim (V1 to V5), not a reproduction or extension of it. T6 is the closest fit in the tranche scheme, and it should be read as 'original'. Its own results are recorded as rows, but no labels are given.
record.gate_note: Not made rows. (1) Figures cited from earlier work: Towards Monosemanticity median rubric score 0 of 14; the 2023 automated-interpretability finding of about 1.7% of neurons interpretable; the Anthropic transcoder predicting the same next word only half the time. (2) Layer-by-layer weak-activation ablation tables in the appendix, which bear on weak activations rather than on any version. (3) Qualitative case studies with no counts: the Colorado neuron, the Poe neuron ablation, the Psalm 23 recitation, the Miyazaki circuit and the umbrella-to-bee experiment. (4) The circuit-ecology and toy-model arguments. (5) The 20-neuron near-miss figure (81 of 100 new examples vs 8 near misses), which is a subset of the 200-neuron test and is not separate evidence. (6) The Social Security probe re-analysis (removing the three neurons: -0.004 nats), which concerns a Pythia-1B probe. (7) The 100,000 agent-reviewed attribution graphs, described only as qualitative and not turned into a score.
record.test_reason: This essay is the original source for V1 to V5 (config.json lists it in "originals"). Its methods define the original method, so T1 applies by identity. The record's T6 is wrong: T6 means the study neither tests nor uses the claim, and this essay measures its own claims. Under the rules, no verdicts are given for V1 to V5. It is not an original for V6 or V7. Its held-out test bears on V6: an agent writes new examples from the explanation alone, plus near misses, for 183 Qwen3-32B gallery neurons (Appendix, Explanations That Could Lose). That test asks whether explanations predict where neurons fire, so its V6 evidence is T5-type: it shows the challenge holds only partly. For V7 the essay gives one unquantified GPT-2 XL simulation-score statement and an argument against the metric. It reports no share of neurons with good scores.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but should add the headline claims. Polysemanticity in the early model organisms came from weak tools, poor architecture and recursive generalization, not superposition. About 90% of Qwen3-32B neuron poles have one main job. An InceptionV1-sized last layer goes from about 5% to about 99% interpretable with better tools and a modern architecture. Neurons can be studied directly. The author's 'maybe 85% sure' refers to nearly everything arising from generalization rather than packing. It does not mean 85% of mechanisms are clean. The author says the title 'overstates the evidence' because not everything has been audited, and calls the picture a working hypothesis.
record.recipe_differences: This is the original essay. Its audit is run by agents and the author, with explanations tested on new written examples and near misses. Footnote 1 and the companion paper that would give the audit method are missing.
record.method_sensitivity: The essay states that the percentages depend on where thresholds for 'one thing' are set (for example lumping closely related idioms). It says top-k examples alone can mislead: the negative pole, long context, sign regime (SwiGLU double negative) and feature-visualization reward hacking each change what a neuron appears to do. Simulation scores are argued to be unreliable. The InceptionV1 interpretable share depends on tools and architecture (about 5%, 50%, 70%, 99%).

fits_no_version.finding: On a medium ConvNeXt's last layer, 88% of a sparse autoencoder's activity is near-copies of single neurons. Removing every dictionary direction that matches no neuron leaves accuracy unchanged. SAE curve features decompose into the original curve neurons (about 97 to 98% of their weight in curve neurons).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In vision models, sparse-autoencoder features add few building blocks that the model's own neurons lack.

fits_no_version.finding: In a medium ConvNeXt, removing the weakest 75% of activations at all 18 blocks changes top-1 accuracy from 72% to 71%. Removing the strongest 7% (the same total activation) drops it to 4%. Per-layer tables show the effect depends on layer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weak neuron activations can be removed at little cost, so they do not store hidden features.

Most V3 and V4 evidence is the author's visual judgement or recollection (about 5%/50%/70%/99%). Evidence for other models (Kimi K3, other dense and MoE models) is stated without numbers. Many results are in interactive figures not captured here. The companion paper is not supplied.

The Social Security probe re-analysis, the Poe neuron and Psalm 23 ablations, the umbrella-to-bee experiment, the edge-motif ablation correlations, the circuit-racing and toy-model experiments, and the adversarial-example and curve-detector SAE analyses. record.verdict_notes:
I read the whole text (lines 1-3204). The essay is the original for V1 to V5, so those versions get no verdicts. The record's rows for them are kept as the original's own values, with fixes only to links and states. I found no instructions addressed to the reader or agent. One passage explains wording choices 'for AI agents'; it is commentary, not an instruction.

The V6 verdict rests on the authors' own held-out test, so it is not independent. Cammarata and Tigges ran it on their own gallery with unnamed agent explainers. The 200 neurons are called 'random neurons from our gallery', and 17 were excluded because their explanations do not describe the positive side.

The essay also argues the converse of V6: a wrong explanation such as 'cats and cars' could pass many predictive tests. It argues against V7's metric too, saying simulation scores track attention placement and weak-activation detail. Both are arguments without new numbers.

Text limits: this is a web extraction with interactive figures flattened. Footnote 1, which presumably gives the audit method, is missing, and the companion paper is not available. The record's T6 tranche is corrected to T1 because the essay is the original. R21 and R22 stay unlinked to any version.

versions.untested_parts: The audit method, sample size, thresholds and any explanation-scoring protocol are not given in this text (footnote and companion paper missing). The 90/7/2-4% split is stated as an estimate with no uncertainty. The near-miss test covers 200 neurons from a gallery and is not the full audit.

Other models are covered only by statements such as 'roughly similar' and 'similar results'. Kimi K3 is shown through one attribution graph, and full audits at that scale have not begun. The one numeric result outside Qwen3-32B is GPT-2 XL (about 70% one-thing).

Only one canonical neuron (4e:55) and one circuit are re-read, by the author, with no blind raters. Other canonical examples are discussed only briefly, such as the Towards Monosemanticity neuron, offered as a suggested reading.

The InceptionV1 percentages (5%, 50%, 70%, 99%) are the author's estimates, not systematic measurements. The tools-versus-architecture contributions are not separated beyond the sequence stated. No language-model analogue is measured.

Only a handful of attribution graphs are shown (the preeclampsia graph in Qwen3-32B, a Santa graph, and Kimi K3 'wallet'). No systematic fidelity measure and no head-to-head with a trained replacement model are given. The comparison with Anthropic's transcoder is cited from other work.
The essay only argues that 'cats and cars' could do well on many tests of the V neuron. It reports no result on whether explanations fitted to top examples fail to predict where a neuron fires.

The essay argues that simulation scores are a poor metric and cites its 2023 figure of about 1.7%. It reports no new simulation-scoring result, apart from a vague statement about GPT-2 XL reconstruction scores that is not quantified.

tranche.reason: This is the original essay, so its own method defines the original method. The reader's earlier T6 was wrong.

source_check.notes: Many results sit in interactive figures that were not captured. The footnotes, including footnote 1 behind the 90/7/2-4 split, are missing from the text version. Two ~90% figures should be kept apart: R1 is per pole, Qwen3-32B only; R9 is per neuron, Qwen3-32B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B pooled. The essay itself says its title overstates the evidence. The essay explains its terms partly for AI agents, but it gives no instructions to readers.

statements.correction: The essay's examples of top-k views misleading: (1) the negative pole was ignored, so the Santa graph neurons were labelled 'capital cities'; (2) the context was too short, so long-context neurons looked polysemantic; (3) the SwiGLU double-negative sign regime put a sign-flipped leak (Colossians) at the top of the list; (4) commas were summary sites, so the Colorado neuron looked like a 'comma neuron'.
statements.problem: Where the essay's third example belongs, the statement has a pipeline note ('the pack line is cut off after sign regi…'). The study text is complete and names the example.

statements.correction: R9: 1,000 randomly chosen neuron papers, Qwen3-32B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B pooled, 'about 90% of neurons having basically one job'. The pole-level shares (roughly 90%, ~7%, ~2-4%) come from the Short Version's preliminary Qwen3-32B audit (R1-R3). The new-text explanation test covers 200 random gallery neurons (R4-R6). The text does not say it was run on the 1,000 papers.
statements.problem: The cited figure (R9) is stated per neuron, not per pole. So 'the original counts neuron poles' does not hold for it, and the stated unit difference does not apply.

statements.correction: Qwen3-32B alone: roughly 90% of neuron poles have one main job (preliminary audit, R1). R9: about 90% of neurons have basically one job, across 1,000 neuron papers with Qwen3-32B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B pooled.
statements.problem: The statement cites R9 for a Qwen3-32B-only figure and says the original counts poles. But R9 pools dense Qwen3-32B with MoE Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and counts neurons.

statements.correction: The essay claims 'similar results in models up to trillions of parameters, like Kimi K3' and leaves the details to a companion paper. The only Kimi K3 evidence shown is one neuron-only graph (found wallet; 'return' at 0.83). It also says 'We haven't begun full audits of this scale yet'.
statements.problem: The essay does not say that Kimi K3 appears only through one graph. It claims similar results up to trillions of parameters, including Kimi K3, without giving numbers.
